questions.question: Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a multi-sport event held every ________ years among athletes from all over Asia.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Asian Games, also known as Asiad, is a multi-sport event held every **four**__ years among athletes from all over Asia.
 
• The most recent one was held in Palembang and Jakarta, Indonesia from 18 August-2 September 2018.
 
• The next games will be held from 10 to 25 September 2022 in China.

questions.question: The base financial year for the calculation of the all India Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is:
questions.solution:
__
 
• The base financial year for the calculation of the all India Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is **2011-2012**__.
 
• IIP index shows the performance of different industrial sectors of the economy of India.
 
• It is published on a monthly basis by CSO (Central Statistical Organisation).

questions.question: The Qutub Minar was named after the Sufi saint ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Qutub Minar was named after the Sufi saint **Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki**__.
 
• The foundation stone for it was laid by Qutub-ud-Din Aibak, while Iltutumish got it completed.
 
• The monument is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Delhi.
 
• It has 5 storeys and is 73 m tall.
 
• Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki was a Sufi saint of the Chishti order from Delhi.

questions.question: ________ won gold in the Men’s freestyle wrestling 65 kg category at the Dan Kolov 2019 wrestling event.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Bajrang Punia**__ won gold in the Men’s freestyle wrestling 65 kg category at the Dan Kolov 2019 wrestling event.
 
• Pooja Dhanda won gold in the 59 kg category at the event held in Russia.
 
• Sakshi Malik claimed a silver medal in the 65 kg category.

questions.question: The Almatti dam project on the Krishna river was an issue between which states?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Almatti dam project on the Krishna river was an issue between **Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra**__.
 
• It is a hydroelectric project situated in the Bagalkot district, North Karnataka.
 
• It was chosen for the World Bank’s Award of Excellence for best utilization of funds for renovation in order to increase the strength of the dam.

questions.question: ________ built the world famous Harmandar Sahib, popularly known as the Golden Temple in Amritsar.
questions.solution:
• **Guru Arjan Sahib**, the Fifth Nanak, **conceived the idea of creating a central place of worship for the Sikhs** and he himself designed the architecture of Sri Harmandir Sahib.
 
• The planning to excavate the Amrit Sarovar was chalked out by **Guru Amardas Sahib**, the Third Nanak, but it was executed by **Guru Ramdas** Sahib under the supervision of Baba Budha Ji.
 
• The land for the site was acquired by the earlier Guru Sahibs on payment or free of cost from the Zamindars (landlords) of native villages.
 
• It is an important pilgrimage site for Sikhs.
 
• The temple is plated with gold.
 
• It is built around a Sarovar which was completed by Guru Ram Das in 1577.

questions.question: ________ is an important road link between Srinagar on one side and Kargil and Leh on the other side.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Zoji La**__ is an important road link between Srinagar on one side and Kargil and Leh on the other side.
 
• It separates Kashmir valley and Dras valley.
 
• After Fotu La, it is the second-highest pass on the Srinagar-Leh National Highway.

questions.question: During whose reign did the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visit India?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visited India during the reign of **Harshavardhana**__.
 
• He is also known as the Prince of Pilgrims.
 
• Harshavardhana ruled North India from 606-647 CE. He was the ruler of the Vardhana dynasty.
 
• Chandragupta Vikramaditya, Chandragupta I, and Samudragupta were all the rulers of the Gupta dynasty.

questions.question: Flying Officer ________ of the Indian Air Force (IAF) created history by becoming the first Indian woman to fly her first solo fighter flight in a Russian made MiG-21 fighter.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Flying Officer **Avani Chaturvedi**__ of the Indian Air Force (IAF) created history by becoming the first Indian woman to fly her first solo fighter flight in a Russian made MiG-21 fighter. 
 
• Bhawana Kanth and Mohana Singh will also fly the same flight soon.
 
• The trio was inducted in the IAF in 2016.

questions.question: Who decides on the issue related to the disqualification of a Member of Lok Sabha under Tenth Schedule?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The **Speaker**__ decides on the issue related to the disqualification of a Member of Lok Sabha under Tenth Schedule.
 
• The 10th Schedule of the Indian Constitution is also known as Anti-Defection Law.
 
• It was inserted by the 52nd Amendment in 1985.
 
• Defection means to abandon an association or position.

questions.question: The theory that dinosaurs were driven to extinction by the aftermath of a large asteroid impact on Earth was given by ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The theory that dinosaurs were driven to extinction by the aftermath of a large asteroid impact on Earth was given by **Luis Alvarez**__.
 
• This theory is known as the Alvarez Hypothesis.
 
• Luis Walter Alvarez was an American physicist.
 
• He was awarded Nobel Prize in Physics in 1968.

questions.question: What does the Lorenz Curve indicate?

options.text: Relationship between the price of a certain commodity and its demand

questions.solution:
__
 
• The Lorenz Curve indicates **income distribution**__.
 
• It is a graphical representation of the distribution of wealth or of income.
 
• It was developed in 1905 by Max O. Lorenz to represent inequality of the wealth distribution.

questions.question: In March 2019, the Government of ________ launched the 'Lose to Win' programme to assist overweight employees shed extra kilos and adopt a healthy lifestyle.
questions.solution:
__
 
• In March 2019, the Government of** UAE**__ launched the 'Lose to Win' programme to assist overweight employees shed extra kilos and adopt a healthy lifestyle.
 
• It was launched by its Ministry of Health and Prevention.
 
• The programme team comprises of health educators and nutritionists from the Ministry.

questions.question: Brazilian physicist and astronomer ________ was awarded the 2019 Templeton Prize, worth $1.4 million, for his work blending science and spirituality.
questions.solution:
__
 
• Brazilian physicist and astronomer **Marcelo Gleiser**__ was awarded the 2019 Templeton Prize, worth $1.4 million, for his work blending science and spirituality.
 
• He is the first person from Latin America to win this prize.
 
• The Templeton Prize was started in the year 1972 by a famous investor John Templeton.
 
• Mother Teresa and Dalai Lama have also received it in the past.

questions.question: ________ is famous for outstanding specimen of Buddhist art and architecture, belonging to the period between the 3rd century B.C. and the 12th century A.D.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Sanchi**__ is famous for outstanding specimen of Buddhist art and architecture, belonging to the period between the 3rd century B.C. and the 12th century A.D.
 
• It is famous for its Stupa, situated in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The Great Stupa was commissioned by Ashoka in 3rd century BCE.
 
• It is one of the oldest stones structures of India.

questions.question: In March 2018, Indian actress ________ was named as the new ambassador of the international award-winning non-profit organisation, Educate Girls.
questions.solution:
__
 
• In March 2018, Indian actress **Katrina Kaif__** was named as the new ambassador of the international award-winning non-profit organisation, Educate Girls.
 
• She will attempt to bring renewed focus to gender equality and girl child education.

questions.question: The Suri king ________ defeated Humayun to regain his kingdom.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Suri king **Sher Shah Suri**__ defeated Humayun to regain his kingdom in 1538.
 
• He was the founder of Suri Empire.
 
• He ruled from 1538-1545.
 
• Humayun was the second Mughal Emperor and son of Babur.
 
• Sikandar Shah Suri was the 6th ruler of the Suri Empire.

questions.question: Who invented the atomic battery in 1913?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Henry Moseley**__ invented the atomic battery in 1913.
 
• His battery contained a spherical glass globe with a silver lining.
 
• The glass sphere had an emitter of a radioactive isotope of radium.
 
• The emitted charged particles caused a build-up of charge, which effectively created a radioactively powered capacitor from which an electric current could be extracted.
 
•

questions.question: Who was the Fifth Sikh Gurus?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Guru Arjan Dev**__ was the fifth of the ten Sikh Gurus.
 
• Guru Arjan Dev was executed by Jahangir.
 
• Guru Arjan Dev is known and remembered as the founder of Golden Temple.
 
• Guru Nanak Dev Ji was the first Guru of Sikhs.
 
• The 10th and the last Guru was Guru Gobind Singh Ji.
 
• Guru Angad was second, Guru Hargobind was sixth, and Guru Ramdas was the fourth Guru.

questions.question: In March 2019, a science teacher from rural Kenya named ________ won the prestigious Global Teacher Prize 2019, worth $1 million, which honours the world’s best teacher.
questions.solution:
__
 
• In March 2019, a science teacher from rural Kenya named **Peter Tabichi**__ won the prestigious Global Teacher Prize 2019, worth $1 million, which honours the world’s best teacher.
 
• He is a physics and maths teacher and was awarded for his achievements in a deprived school with a few textbooks and crowded classes.
 
• He teaches at Keriko Secondary school and gives away 80% of his income for helping poor students.
